description: Article-based learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway.

cards.title: The Most Obvious Realities Are Hardest to See
cards.subtitle: 'How's the water?' 'What the hell is water?'
body: Fish don't know they're in water—it's too constant to notice.
Same for humans. The beliefs and patterns that shape everything are invisible because they're everywhere.
cards.takeaway: What's most pervasive is often least visible.

cards.title: Education Teaches How to Think
cards.subtitle: The real value isn't facts—it's choosing what to pay attention to.
body: A liberal arts education gives you control over your own attention and interpretation.
You decide what has meaning. Most people never exercise the option.
cards.takeaway: Education's real gift is conscious choice over how you interpret experience.

cards.title: Your Default Is Self-Centeredness
cards.subtitle: You're at the center of your universe—but so is everyone else.
body: Every experience you've ever had has happened to you. You're the center. This is how consciousness works.
But every other person experiences the same thing. You're a background character in their story.
cards.takeaway: Everyone is the protagonist of their own story.

cards.title: Adult Life Is Tedious Routine
cards.subtitle: The grocery store. The commute. The waiting.
body: Not dramatic crises—just low-grade frustration on repeat.
How you handle the boring, frustrating parts is how you handle life.
cards.takeaway: The mundane is where most of life actually happens.

cards.title: In Traffic, Everyone's in Your Way
cards.subtitle: Your default: these people are obstacles.
body:
• The SUV that cut you off
• The slow driver
• The person who took your spot
Your automatic response is irritation. That interpretation is optional—it just doesn't feel optional.
cards.takeaway: Frustration feels like fact but it's actually interpretation.

cards.title: You Can Choose Different Stories
cards.subtitle: That SUV might be rushing to a hospital.
body: You don't know why people do what they do. You're making up a story.
Neither story is provably true. One makes your life harder.
cards.takeaway: Stories about others are fabrications—you might as well choose kinder ones.

cards.title: Awareness Requires Constant Effort
cards.subtitle: Your default mode is autopilot, not conscious choice.
body: Staying aware, questioning automatic responses—this is exhausting.
Freedom takes work. Continuous, daily work.
cards.takeaway: Conscious living is effortful; autopilot is the default.

cards.title: Worship Something—You Don't Get to Not
cards.subtitle: Everyone worships. The only choice is what.
body:
• Worship money = never enough
• Worship body = always ugly
• Worship intellect = always fraudulent
These aren't evil—they're just insatiable masters.
cards.takeaway: Whatever you organize your life around will eventually own you.

cards.title: Real Hell Is Unconscious Living
cards.subtitle: The same routine forever, with no awareness that anything else is possible.
body: Hell isn't fire—it's the rat race with no sense that you chose any of it.
The alternative isn't escaping routine. It's being awake within it.
cards.takeaway: Unconscious routine is its own kind of death.

cards.title: Real Freedom Is Attention
cards.subtitle: You control what you notice and what meaning you assign.
body: You can't control what happens. You can control how you interpret it.
This is the only real freedom. Everything else is in service of this or hollow.

cards.title: Clichés Are True
cards.subtitle: 'It's about the journey, not the destination.' Eye-roll. But correct.
body: The truest things have been said so often they've become invisible.
The trick is to actually live them. Hearing truth and living truth are years apart.
cards.takeaway: Clichés point at real things we've stopped seeing.

cards.title: This Is Water
cards.subtitle: The obvious is invisible. The choice is yours.
body: The water is still there. The routine doesn't change.
What changes is whether you're conscious. This is water. Will you notice it?
cards.takeaway: Awareness of the obvious is the work of a lifetime.
